title: Omit Keys
prompt: A TypeScript serializer needs to remove sensitive fields before logging an object. Write a function that returns a shallow copy without any keys listed in the keys array.

explanation.beginner:
Example: omitKeys({"id":1,"password":"secret"}, ["password"]) produces {"id":1}. The result must follow this precise rule: A TypeScript serializer needs to remove sensitive fields before logging an object. Write a function that returns a shallow copy without any keys listed in the keys array. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “omits multiple keys”: input [{"a":1,"b":2,"c":3},["a","c"]] produces {"b":2}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.

Tempting mistake: Do not hard-code the first example: the omits multiple keys case changes the input contract’s boundary or shape. Compare the actual outputs rather than only checking whether both are truthy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.
